sutta: Dhamma. 41.9 On that occasion the naked ascetic Kassapa who in lay life had been an old friend of Citta the householder arrived in Macchikasanda. Citta the householder heard about this and approached the naked ascetic Kassapa. He exchanged greetings with him and when they had concluded the greetings and cordial talk he sat down to one side and said to him, "How long has it been venerable Kassapa since you went forth?" "It has been 30 years householder since I went forth. In these 30 years venerable sir have you attained any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones the Aryans any dwelling in comfort?" And he said, "In these 30 years since I went forth householder I have not attained any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones no dwelling in comfort but only nakedness and the shaven head and the brush for cleaning my seat." Stop here for a moment. So this uh Kassapa is an old friend of Citta. and he has renounced for 30 years as a naked ascetic, and now he came back to Majjhima Sanda, and uh he acknowledged that he did not attain any Aryan uh stage, any supernormal stage, uh but he only had this nakedness, uh the shaven head, the bowl, head, and the brush for cleaning the seat. What is this brush for cleaning the seat? Cuz he goes around naked, so every time he wants to sit on the ground, you know, these ascetics, when they go to the forest, they go anywhere, they have to sit on the ground, uh. So, when he sits on the ground, uh, his backside, uh, is exposed, uh, the pebbles and the stones will prick his backside, uh. Uh, so he has to use the brush to clean away all the big stones, so that, uh, he can sit without, uh, being poked by all the stones, uh. And this was said, Cittala the householder said to him, "It is a wonderful indeed, sir. It's amazing indeed, sir, how well expounded is the Dhamma, in that after 30 years you have not attained any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, nor dwelling in comfort, but only nakedness and the shaven head and the brush for cleaning your seat." So, Cittala was surprised that the Buddha's Dhamma-vinaya is so good, and that a person can attain this, uh, Aryan stage, but this naked ascetic, after suffering for 30 years as a naked ascetic, uh, and still had attained nothing, uh. And then, uh, Kassapa asked him, "But, householder, how long has it been since you became a lay follower, I mean, a lay follower of the Buddha?" "In my case, too, venerable sir, it has been 30 years." "In these 30 years, householder, have you attained any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones and a dwelling in comfort? And Chitta said, "How could I not, venerable sir? For to whatever extent I wish, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I enter and dwell in the first jhana, which is accompanied by thought directed and sustained with delight and happiness born of seclusion. Then to whatever extent I wish, with the subsiding of thought directed and sustained, I enter and dwell in the second jhana. Then to whatever extent I wish, with the fading away as well of delight, I enter and dwell in the third jhana. Then to whatever extent I wish, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, I enter and dwell in the fourth jhana. Further, if I were to die before the Blessed One does, it would not be surprising if the Blessed One were to declare of me, "There is no factor bound by which Chitta the householder could return to this world." And this was said. I stop here for a moment. So, Chitta is saying that he can attain the four jhanas, which are considered superhuman states, supernormal. Uttari manussa dhamma, supernormal states, which a normal person cannot attain. Also, Chitta says if he were to die, the Buddha would say that he is a non-returner. He will not come back to this human world, will not be reborn in this human world. And this was said. The naked ascetic Kassapa said to Chitta the householder, "It is wonderful indeed, sir. It is amazing indeed, sir, how well expounded in the is the dhamma, in that a layman clothed in white can attain a superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a dwelling in comfort. May I receive the going forth in this Dhamma-Vinaya? May I receive the higher ordination? Oh, he's so impressed that Kassapa, even as a layman, enjoying the family life, can attain such high states, whereas he is suffering as a naked ascetic, and yet cannot attain anything. So, he asked Citta to bring him to ordain. Then Citta, the householder, took the naked ascetic Kassapa to the elder monks and said to them, "Venerable sirs, this naked ascetic Kassapa is an old friend of ours from lay life. Let the elders give him the going forth. Let them give him the higher ordination. I will be zealous in providing him robes, alms food, lodging, and medicinal requisites." Then the naked ascetic Kassapa received the going forth in this Dhamma-Vinaya. He received the higher ordination, and soon, not long after his higher ordination, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, Venerable Kassapa, by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life, entered and dwelt in that unsurpassed goal of the holy life, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness. He directly knew, "Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done. There is no more for this state of being." And the Venerable Kassapa became one of the arahants. So, here he says, "Soon, not long after his higher ordination, he attained arahantship." This "soon, not long after his higher ordination" will be at least a few years, huh? Because normally he has to train under a teacher for at least 5 years. And then, after that, he's allowed to go and live alone, and do his uh work very hard now to attain liberation. So, normally during even during the Buddha's time, monks would take at least more than 10 years or 20 years and then become arahants. But, there are of course exceptions like Sariputta and Moggallana and Mahakassapa and all that.
